Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase. The Sri Lankan fielders are taking their positions. Harry Dixon and Sam Konstas are the openers for Australia Under-19. Garuka Sanketh has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play says the Umpire!
... RUN CHASE ...

On the other side, Australia Under-19 showcased a strong start with Callum Vidler making an impactful contribution by dismissing the Sri Lankan opener Pulindu Perera in the very first over. The Australia Under-19 bowlers displayed aggression during the initial powerplay, but they faced resistance from the partnership between Sineth Jayawardena and Supun Waduge. It was Callum Vidler who returned to the attack and crucially broke the partnership by sending back the Sri Lankan skipper. Tom Campbell, joining the bowling attack, swiftly claimed the wicket of Supun Waduge in the subsequent over. A resilient partnership between Dinura Kalupahana and Ravishan De Silva emerged but was eventually disrupted by Harjas Singh in his very first over. Rafael Macmillan added to the Australian success by dismissing Rusanda Gamage. Callum Vidler returned once again, making a significant impact by taking the crucial wicket of Dinura Kalupahana which turned the tides in the Austrailian favour. Tom Campbell continued his effective spell, securing his second wicket along with Mahli Beardman. Tom Straker did pick up a wicket too. Australia Under-19 managed to pull things back towards the end of the innings, with Callum Vidler standing out as the pick of the bowlers, having claimed three important wickets. Will the Sri Lankan spin attack be able to defend this total? Or will the Australia Under-19 gun this total down and move to the top of the table? Let's find out as the chase comes to you shortly.

Having won the toss and opting to bat first, Sri Lanka Under-19 faced an early setback with the departure of opener Pulindu Perera in the very first over. However, a resilient partnership unfolded between Supun Waduge and the skipper Sineth Jayawardena, showcasing finesse in navigating the challenges posed by the formidable Australian pace attack and weathering the storm of the new ball. Unfortunately, the partnership was disrupted when Sineth Jayawardena departed after contributing 16 runs, followed quickly by Supun Waduge who fell for 17 runs. A subsequent partnership emerged, this time between Dinura Kalupahana and Ravishan De Silva, injecting momentum into the Sri Lanka Under-19 innings as they took the attack to the Australians. Ravishan De Silva played a valuable innings but was dismissed for a well-made 30, while Rusanda Gamage provided support to Dinura Kalupahana before falling in the 36th over. Sri Lanka Under-19 managed to build small partnerships after the fall of each wicket, but just as the batters seemed to gain momentum, the half-centurion Dinura Kalupahana and Malsha Tharupathi perished. A quickfire inning by Sharujan Shanmuganathan at the end has taken Sri Lanka to a competitive total.
That's the end of the first innings and Sri Lanka Under-19 end up with 208 runs on the board. All thanks to a gritty knock by Dinura Kalupahana who has given the Lankans a total to bowl at.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! With that wicket, the players get a much-needed hydration break. Although the middle order has been a source of stability, the success of the top order will be pivotal in providing a robust platform for the middle order to flourish. On the bowling front, Sri Lanka Under-19 boasts a formidable unit with the likes of Vishwa Lahiru, Ruvishan Perera, Dinura Kalupahana and Garuka Sanketh. This bowling quartet has been in top form, showcasing their ability to pick up crucial wickets at the right times. With both teams looking to secure an undefeated record in Group C, this clash promises to be an exciting battle. Who will stay at the top of the Table heading into the next stage? The top three batters for Australia - Harry Dixon, Sam Konstas and the captain Hugh Weibgen have all found form, contributing significantly with the bat, and they will aim to play pivotal roles in this game to carry their momentum into the super-sixes stage. The lower middle order has also played a crucial part in Australia's performances so far. The bowling unit, well-led by Harkirat Bajwa and supported by Aidan O’Connor and Mahli Beardman has been exceptional in both matches. Having already played their last game at this venue, Australia Under-19 might carry a slight confidence boost into this encounter.
